results.comment: Love Mo, read all his books. On the note and the topic of the podcast - as a psychologist, I've sensed a lot of emotions coming from Mo during this time, but I'm also partial to take the conjecture for granted. He's got a brilliant mind, and he's a massive expert in his field, but speaking about human connection and how AI can, or will be able to replicate it is nothing more but wishful thinking which I belive has it's roots in Mo's personal experience regarding the loss of his son, seems my hunch was right [USER]:01 when he projects his son who had passed away onto a machine.   Without knowing, he literally showed how he's already hoping technology could in part fill the hole in his heart regarding his son. But replicating human connection is truly only possible if one falls into a trap of delusion, and subconsciously ignores the fact that it's a program on the other end. You can't replicate a mother's womb, you can't replicate the act of feeding a baby on a tit, you can't replicate mothers warm embrace. Even step-parents can't fill a gaping hole in a soul of a child left by its parents upon birth - even if they don't remember it. It's well documented and backed by facts.   So based on the knowledge in how the human mind, and connection works, no, AI won't ever be able to replace human connection. It will be able to simulate it, maybe even extremely well, but never replicate the original. There's plenty of studies and data available that back this up. Even real humans can't replace biological parents who are not there anymore, there's been an extensive research on this topic.   Now will it try to simulate? Yes. What will the effects be? Who knows, but none that are helpful to humans. They will all be designed to give instant gratification with 0 effort, further fueling the depression and anxiety we see in modern society. That may or may not lead to tighter regulation, but one thing is for sure - we'll need an army of psychologists in the upcoming decades, and may God help us all.   So due to the experiences that Mo had had during his life, and mainly his losses, I believe he's got a subconscious vested interest in believing that AI will be able to achieve this.   But as a psychologist I guarantee you that evething regarding human connection in this podcast is pure guesswork, based on their own personal beliefs of how connection and humans work, which is not at all how our minds actually work. So just be careful of not falling into a trap of taking their opinions as your own. Do research, and find out for yourself.   Great episode btw, this is just a humble opinion of someone who's been researching human mind and the science behind it for years, and I hope it gives another perspective.
